reviews.review_msg: she is a nice professor and I get what she's trying to do by making the assignments "fun" but in reality her mini projects are very confusing and way more work than just doing "regular" psych assignments. it's too time consuming and i don't think anyone is enjoying pretending to be an alien. her lectures are also very boring and content is stale.

Nice prof but always underplayed the difficulty of assignments, "just do x," and TAs would mark harsher than she states. Often 5-10 mins late, lectures were 110+ slides and she usually didn't get through them all. Not her fault, but content was quite boring and she overexplained concepts with overusing in-class demonstrations

Dr. Xie is quite engaging and provides many modes of interactive learning throughout class, did drag on a bit sometimes, but 3 hour classes often do. The rubrics were detailed, but unfortunately the TAs did not provide very detailed feedback as to how they landed on the grade you received and were not always super responsive.

Great prof, had a super unique assignment that was basically a social game. Attendance is necessary if you want free marks. Only issue is the required method of contacting the prof and TAs was through a discussion board, and some questions weren't answered for 10+ days & after the due date passed. Other than that, super personable and friendly :)

Lectures are slow/dragged on. Assignments do not have a clear criteria and sometimes is given after assignments have been graded. You are graded on 4 mini projects + the final project/exam. The feedback for all these projects (except the first), including the final project draft, did not get released until a day before the final project is due.

Very solid instructor. Social cognition material was a bit dry but she did her best to make it fun and engaging. If you attend lectures and do the readings, you should do fine. I learned a lot, but didn't do as well I'd hoped.

Sally was great! I'm nearing the end of my semester with her. My only complaint would be how disorganized some aspects of the course were; sometimes she would show up late or cancel class with very little notice. When I asked direct questions, I did not get direct responses; instead, I was merely directed to external links (which were from the TAs)
The best psychology professor I've had at SFU. If you get a chance to take one of her classes definitely do it!

This class did not deserve Dr. Y. Xie. She was so charismatic and kind, but most university students (myself included) just show up because there is a participation mark. I found the course content pretty dull, but she tried her best to make it engaging. Having no tests was refreshing and allowed for some creativity in the projects.

Very solid instructor. Social cognition material was a bit dry but she did her best to make it fun and engaging. If you attend lectures and do the readings, you should do fine. I learned a lot, but didn't do as well I'd hoped.

She will quickly be recognized as SFU's finest. Sally is so caring and empathetic to the student experience. She constantly asks for student feedback on the course and is flexible with deadlines. She presents concepts in relatable and interesting ways. No exams, just easy quizzes, participation, few assignments, and a final paper. She's awesome!
